challenge.method: Checked whether the generic HTML title could identify an earlier UK edition or the Welsh v3 representation. Compared the language attribute, body version declaration, footer routes and neighboring Index rows. Tested whether active alone selected v3.
challenge.results: The English /version/3/ page explicitly declares version 3.0 and links other editions and the Welsh page separately. The publisher preserves prior-version terms for existing uses. UK v1.0 and v2.0 also have active Index rows, so the opaque ID, edition and witness digest are necessary to select this reference.

limitations: The footer links a separate Welsh representation. Its bytes and equivalence are outside this English witness review.

A work-specific finding requires evidence that an authorized provider offered the material under this licence. Attribution conditions and exemptions, including personal data and unauthorized third-party rights, constrain reuse. Redistribution and installation require separate assessment.
The Index decision governs documentary lookup. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation and authorization for a consumer dataset release remain separate questions.
reasoning: The National Archives’ English HTML identifies version 3.0 and describes its development as a common licence for public-sector information. Its operative grant covers expressly offered copyright and database-right material, including data. The Index taxonomy admits that grant as a license and the exact UK v3.0 row assigns active.
